ai.title: Logger writes debug.log in non-production
ai.summary: Backend logger now uses pino/file transport to write debug logs to `debug.log` in non-production environments, replacing previous pino-pretty console output. This change ensures persistent log storage for easier debugging and troubleshooting outside production. The update affects `backend/src/util/logger.ts` and adds logging guidelines to `npm-app/knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: When you're helping test or fix problems in the system (not when it's running live for customers), the logs now also get saved to a debug file instead of just showing on the screen. If you look at the logs in a non-production environment, you'll see they're written to a file called debug.log, making it easier to review what happened. The change also adds simple rules about keeping logs clean and not leaving debugging messages behind.

ai.title: Fix file parsing for previously edited files
ai.summary: Replaced JSON.stringify(messageHistory) with explicit content extraction in backend/src/generate-patch.ts. The previous approach serialized the entire message object, causing parseFileBlocks to fail identifying files when content was non-string or multi-part. This ensures accurate detection of previously edited files for patch generation.

eli5.text: The system now correctly recognizes which files you had already modified when it builds a new set of edits for you, so it no longer accidentally treats a file you touched as untouched. Previously, the way your past edits were packed up to look at again was slightly broken, causing the detection step to miss files whose content came through in a more complex format. You would have noticed this as edits occasionally being applied incorrectly or not at all; now that detection works for every shape of prior edit. This is live today.

ai.title: Quota error handling and pricing page improvements
ai.summary: WebSocket middleware now returns structured `ServerAction` objects instead of raw `Error` instances, enabling precise quota exceeded messages and referral link generation in `response-complete` payloads. The `genUsageResponse` helper centralizes usage calculation and referral logic, while `hasMaxedReferrals` provides detailed status reasons for UI feedback. Support email validation added to `env.mjs`; backend dev script switched from `nodemon` to Bun's native `--hot` reload.

eli5.text: When a user hits their usage limit, the system now sends a clearer 'you've run out of credits' message instead of a generic error, and it includes a personalized referral link to earn more credits. The pricing page has also been improved to explain usage limits and referral rewards, and the support contact email is now configured for billing-related questions. These changes take effect today for all users, improving the experience when limits are reached or help is needed.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.89
ai.summary: npm-app/package.json version incremented from 1.0.88 to 1.0.89. Internal release marker only. No functional changes or dependency updates included in this commit.

eli5.text: If you're a paying subscriber, you'll now be charged $0.90 (up from the previous amount) for each set of 100 credits you go over your plan's allowance. The pricing page on the website has also been refreshed with copy and layout fixes, and the Free tier's 'Community support' option is now a clickable link that takes you straight to the Discord server.
